rationale: bugs_open/292, found as a PRE-FLIGHT for the Phase C pilot rather than after a symptom: matchVerticalDirectory (feed_directory_recommendation_action.go) decides whether a site should carry a provider directory, and its DOMAIN-derived signal was collected by ranging verticalDirectoryMap and appending EVERY match, while the dispatch loop below returns on the FIRST exact match. Go randomises map iteration, and this map DELIBERATELY mixes recommending entries (mortgage/savings/banking/insurance/health insurance) with a not-recommending one ('finance' — too generic to choose a provider class, and a wrong directory is worse than none). So a domain containing two keywords on opposite sides resolved DIFFERENTLY RUN TO RUN. This is not hypothetical and not merely theoretical for some future domain: mortgage-refinance.co.uk sits in the portfolio register's M4 entry — the same entry as the Phase C pilot — and 'refinance' contains 'finance', so it matched both 'mortgage' (recommended) and 'finance' (not). A test asserting the correct outcome FAILED ON ITERATION 1 against the unfixed code (Recommended=false, kind="") and passes 600x3 after the fix. The sharpest part, and the reason this is also a 016b Sec 9 entry: the file ALREADY KNOWS about the hazard — the partial-match arm twenty lines below carries a comment stating that map order is random and that this map mixes verdicts, and picks the longest key for exactly that reason. The guard was written for the inner case and the outer case was left, so a grep for the hazard lands on the comment and stops. FIX: append AT MOST ONE domain-derived keyword, chosen by the same rule the partial matcher already uses (longest key wins, lexicographic tie-break). Longest-wins is the RIGHT answer, not merely a stable one: the specific provider class is what a remortgage site needs, and 'finance' is not-recommended precisely because it is too generic to pick one. Explicit classification signals still precede any domain-derived one, pinned by a second test. DAMAGE TO DATE IS ZERO and measured as such: the flag is only reachable through the two consumers wired by migration 432, improvement-sweep has been disabled fleet-wide since 2026-08-14, and a census shows ZERO sites carrying any finance content_features key. This is a defect caught before it produced damage. Had it fired, it would have been invisible: recommended:false means NO WRITE by design, so the absence is indistinguishable from 'never evaluated', and the discovery checks gate on the flag being PRESENT, so a site that never got the flag is never reported as missing its directory.

plan.summary: bugs_open/292: make matchVerticalDirectory's domain-derived signal deterministic. It ranged a mixed-verdict map (randomised order) and appended every match into a first-match-wins dispatch, so a domain containing two opposite keywords flipped per run. Append at most one, by the longest-key rule the partial matcher already uses. Plus a regression test that iterates (map order is randomised per range statement, so one run passes by luck).
plan.risks: (1) Behaviour CHANGE for any domain matching 2+ keywords: previously random, now always the longest/most specific. For the one live instance (mortgage-refinance.co.uk) that means mortgage-lender instead of a coin flip — the intended answer. No domain loses a recommendation it deterministically had: single-keyword domains are untouched (pinned by test). (2) A domain matching two RECOMMENDING keywords (e.g. one containing both 'savings' and 'insurance') now deterministically picks the longer — previously random. That is an improvement in kind, but it is a policy choice made by string length, and the honest read is that no such domain exists in the register today; a future one should get an explicit classification signal rather than rely on this tie-break. Stated rather than hidden. (3) Go change: INERT until the next fleet roll — the running binary (v1.0.1305) carries the defect. Releases are whole-fleet and owner-run; this lane does not roll. (4) The Phase C pilot (remortgagecalculator.uk) is UNAFFECTED either way — it matches 'mortgage' only, so it is deterministic on both the old and new code; the pilot was not blocked on this.

edits.rationale: The defect and the fix. Collect the domain-derived keyword by longest-match instead of appending all matches in map order. Comment states the reachable instance and points at the test, so the next reader meets the hazard rather than the guard.

Regression test. It ITERATES because map order is randomised per range statement: a single call passes by luck about half the time, so a one-shot test would be a check that cannot reliably fail. Proven against the unfixed code first (failed on iteration 1), which is the only thing that establishes the test can detect the defect at all.

grounded_in: THE DEFECT, REPRODUCED (not reasoned about): against the unfixed code, TestMatchVerticalDirectory_DomainSignalIsDeterministic failed on ITERATION 1 — 'mortgage-refinance.co.uk: Recommended=false (kind ""), want true'. After the fix: ok, -count=3 (600 iterations per case). The wider Directory|Vertical|NewsFeed suite passes.

THE HAZARD IS DOCUMENTED IN THE SAME FUNCTION, on the other arm: 'map iteration order is random, and this map (unlike the news one) mixes recommending and non-recommending entries, so a signal containing two keys (e.g. "insurance finance") would flip between opposite outcomes run to run. Pick the LONGEST matching key (most specific wins ...), with a lexicographic tie-break for determinism.' The fix applies that stated rule to the loop that builds the signal list.

REACHABILITY, computed against the live portfolio register (REGISTER_positioning.md M4) 2026-08-17: mortgage-refinance.co.uk matches BOTH 'mortgage' and 'finance' ('refinance' contains 'finance') => flips. remortgagecalculator.uk / remortgagequotation.co.uk / remortgagequote.uk / fixedmortgagerates.co.uk / adversecreditmortgage.co.uk / loanandmortgagecalculator.co.uk match 'mortgage' only => deterministic. equityreleasecalculator.co.uk matches nothing.

WHY THE DOMAIN SIGNAL IS LOAD-BEARING (measured): all four comparable finance sites carry classification industry NULL and site_type 'interactive-platform', category 'interactive' — none of which is in verticalDirectoryMap. For this family the domain-derived signal is the ONLY one that can fire, so there is no explicit signal to fall back on.

DAMAGE TO DATE IS ZERO, measured not assumed: SELECT over site_specs where aspect='classification' AND is_current AND content_features ?| ARRAY['mortgage_lender_directory','savings_provider_directory','health_insurer_directory'] returns 0. The only content_features directory keys in existence are model_directory/adoption_tracker/protocol_tracker on ai-agent-orchestration.com (plus news_feed on 9 sites).

WHY IT WOULD HAVE BEEN INVISIBLE: the action returns NO WRITE for a not-recommended verdict (feed_directory_recommendation_action.go:178-197) — the deliberate safe default for an opt-in flag — so a mis-verdict leaves a spec indistinguishable from one never evaluated; and MissingDirectoryPageCheck/MissingDirectorySectionCheck gate on directorySpecFlags(recommended), so a site that never received the flag is never reported as missing its directory. No failure row exists anywhere for this class.

PRIOR ART CHECKED: grep over bugs_open/ + bugs_closed/ for matchVerticalDirectory / verticalDirectoryMap / map-iteration-order returns one file — bugs_open/209, which is the SAME PRIMITIVE at a different site (unified_extractor.go:494 resolving a deploy source by ranging a map). Cited as a relation, not a duplicate; a third instance would argue for a lint rule rather than a third bug file.

FILED WITHOUT A 090 RUN, DECLARED (owner ruling 2026-07-31 escape hatch): the defect is reproduced by a failing-then-passing test, reachability is computed against the real register, and the blast radius is one function read in full — there is no 'the cause may live elsewhere' question for the loop to answer. bugs_open/292 states this substitution in its own second section rather than omitting it silently.

The transferable pattern is filed in 016b Sec 9 ('A guard written for the INNER case leaves the OUTER one — and the file's own comment explaining the hazard reads as proof it was handled'), including why grepping for the hazard finds the fix and stops.
